title: What Matters for Cross-Modal Alignment
abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that models trained on different modalities converge toward a shared representation. Related work aligns frozen image and text encoders on natural images without paired data. We test zero-pair alignment on five datasets across four modalities: natural images, environmental audio, chest radiographs, and 3D computed tomography (CT). It succeeds only on COCO and fails on the other four. We analyze the failures and find that alignment must first locate the subspace where the modalities co-vary and then orient the mapping within it. Consistent with previous studies, medical imaging is the hardest case: its shared subspace carries the smallest fraction of the variance. When this fraction is small, alignment needs image-text pairs, and random-matrix theory predicts how many pairs are needed. These findings motivate LightAlign: a few pairs let a ridge regression between two frozen encoders locate and orient the mapping simultaneously, and a classifier fitted only on report text then predicts findings from the mapped images. On 3D CT, LightAlign surpasses models trained end to end on image-report pairs without finding-level labels: with only 200 pairs, LightAlign outperforms CT-CLIP on CT-RATE (0.754 vs. 0.733 AUROC), and with only 100 CT-RATE pairs, it does so on RAD-ChestCT, an out-of-distribution dataset from a different hospital. On CheXpert, it reaches 0.862 mean AUROC with only about 5% as many pairs as models trained on MIMIC-CXR.

title: Motion of a cylinder between parallel plates: complete Stokes resistance and pressure response
abstract: A circular cylinder moving between two parallel plates is the canonical confined problem of two-dimensional Stokes flow. Rotation and translation of the cylinder along the channel become coupled and generate a pressure difference along the channel under zero-net-flux conditions. Existing results use different methods. We develop a completed double-layer boundary integral formulation based on the channel Green function to resolve narrow gaps at arbitrary transverse positions. The channel Green kernels are derived from a Fourier-transformed biharmonic problem, permitting explicit treatment of the free-space singularity, the slowly decaying nearest-wall contribution, and the small-wavenumber limit for accurate kernel evaluation under strong confinement. The boundary integral equation is discretised by a spectrally accurate Nyström scheme on a graded parametrisation, and the pressure jump follows from the zero-wavenumber limit of the streamwise momentum balance. A single linear system yields the full resistance matrix and pressure-jump coefficients for an eccentric cylinder; an additional right-hand side treats imposed net flux. For nonzero coefficients, comparisons with independent COMSOL finite-element simulations show relative differences below \(0.1\%\) for the resistance coefficients and at most \(0.0122\%\) for the pressure-response coefficients and excess hydraulic resistance. Reciprocity, symmetry constraints, and lubrication asymptotics provide additional checks on the numerical results. We track the coupling between rotation and translation and the pressure generated by the cylinder from the channel scale into the lubrication regime, and determine the pressure--flow relation, driving torque and efficiency of the rotating-cylinder pump for asymmetric clearances.

title: Self-assembly of dipolar nanoclusters on an attractive substrate: A coarse-grained simulation approach
abstract: Recently, Thomas et al. [Nanoscale 17, 18291 (2025)] showed that bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi$_{38}$ O$_{45}$ (Boc-L-Phe-O)$_{24}$] form chains when deposited onto gold or pyrolitic graphite substrates. This chain formation is significantly enhanced when the bismuth in the BiO-NCs is partially replaced by cerium through doping. In this work, we study a simplified, coarse-grained model of this process, namely (magnetic) Stockmayer particles in the presence of an attractive substrate. The model is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations. The deposition experiment is mimicked by a rapid quench from high temperature to a low temperature below the bulk coexistence curve. The results are found to be qualitatively similar to the experimental observations reported earlier. In our simulations, we find significant chain formation in the bulk even at rather low concentrations, which is in contrast to the BiO-NCs in ethanol for which dynamic light scattering reveals negligible aggregation in the absence of the substrate. This lends support to a scenario, conjectured in the work of Thomas at al., where the dipole moments are induced by the particle-substrate interaction and hence there is little dipole moment in the bulk. In a second part, we study the system in equilibrium. We consider the scaling of chains, the number of layers populated as a function of two-dimensional density, and we draw analogies to polymers on interfaces, which have been extensively studied over the past decades. Most notably, it is found that the chains behave as self-avoiding walks at low densities, which gives way to rod-like scaling at higher densities.

title: The novelty exposed: ablation, reproducibility and transparency in 40 technical reports of open-weight large language models (LLMs)
abstract: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ from earlier ones; what 40 randomly sampled technical reports claim as new and whether they support it with ablation studies; and what they disclose for reproducibility and transparency. In the library, 39 of the 48 architectures added in 2025 take at least two of their three core blocks from another model, most often Llama, although part of this reflects how the library writes code. In the reports, 19 of 73 architectural or training novelty claims come with a controlled with/without comparison; 4 of 40 reports state more than one training run; 8 rerun the models they compare against under one setup; and 1 discloses data mixture, token count, and compute together. We also looked for known components given new names: none of five candidate cases hid its origin, though we did not study model names. We propose seven reporting rules for LLM release reports and apply them to two reports. We do not judge model quality, and an untested claim may still be true.

title: Probing superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational wave observations
abstract: We investigate superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations. Under the adopted cloud formation and survival conditions, the $\lvert322\rangle\rightarrow\lvert31-1\rangle$ fine transition can imprint phase corrections in the LISA band, while Bohr transitions occurring after the milli-Hertz band observation can be probed through shifts in the merger time. Modeling the coupled cloud-orbit evolution, we find that cloud depletion can begin before resonance and that ionization can advance rather than delay coalescence. For a representative nearby binary, a vacuum injection-recovery analysis yields a cloud-mass-fraction posterior concentrated at $M_c^i/M\lesssim10^{-6}$. Comparing the LISA-predicted coalescence time with a subsequent ground-based measurement provides a complementary test of later cloud evolution. These results motivate complementary searches for ultralight bosons with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations.

title: A Critical Choquard Problem for a Quasilinear Schrödinger Operator with Singular Discontinuous Nonlinearity
abstract: In this article, we study the quasilinear Schrödinger equation $-Δu - Δ\bigl(|u|^{2α}\bigr)\,|u|^{2α-2}u =λ\left(χ_{\{u<b\}} u^{-β}+\left(\int_Ω\frac{H(y,u)}{\left|x-y\right|^μ} dy\right)h(x,u)\right)$ in $Ω$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded domain, $b>0$, $0<μ<2$, $α>\frac12$, $0<β<3$, and $h$ has critical exponential growth with primitive $H$. We show that there is $λ^*_b\in(0,\infty)$ such that the problem has a positive solution if and only if $λ\in(0,λ^*_b]$. For $λ<λ^*_b$, this solution is $g(v_λ)$, where the change of variables $g$ makes the problem semilinear and $v_λ$ is a local minimizer of the transformed energy in $H^1_0(Ω)$. If $h$ satisfies a lower bound at the critical scale $\exp\bigl(2α\,g^{-1}(u)^2\bigr)$, we obtain a second positive solution for every $λ\in(0,λ^*_b)$. The level estimate for this solution must be done at this scale, and not at the scale $e^{u^{4α}}$ used for semilinear problems. This bound excludes $h=f\,e^{u^{4α}}$ with $f$ of polynomial growth. For $α>1$, we obtain a second solution for $h=u^{4α-1}e^{u^{4α}}$, provided that the maximum of the first solution exceeds a constant depending only on $α$. For $α\leq1$, this question remains open.

title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) encode a high-resolution image into thousands of visual tokens, which dominate the cost of the prefill stage. Visual token reduction removes most of these tokens, but two problems remain at extreme budgets. The vision encoder still processes every patch of the image, and the few surviving tokens often miss the small regions that hold the answer. In this paper, we propose Glance-ETD, a two-stage token reduction framework guided by a lightweight question-conditioned scorer. In the first stage, a glance encoder views the image at low resolution and re-encodes only the question-relevant regions at native resolution. In the second stage, Evidence-Tempered Diversity (ETD) selects the final tokens by combining diversity with the evidence predicted by the scorer, so that the kept tokens cover the scene and retain the answer. A single-rollout self-distillation recipe trains the MLLM with the glance encoder. With only 5% of the visual tokens, Glance-ETD retains 91.6% of the full-token performance of Qwen3.5-4B across fourteen benchmarks and outperforms the strongest prior method, LT-OPD, by 17.3 points and the same training recipe with DivPrune by 6.0. It also speeds up the time to first token on 4K images by 3.1x and generalizes to three other MLLMs and to high-resolution document benchmarks, with the largest gains on text-rich tasks.

title: Hidden symmetries and echolocation
abstract: We study the echolocation problem: whether local spectral data determine a point up to isometry. We characterize cospectrality by the existence of a spectral symmetry exchanging the two point evaluations and introduce a pointwise analogue of Sunada's method for constructing such symmetries. This yields cospectral, non-similar points on closed hyperbolic surfaces of every genus at least three and on round lens spaces. We also obtain Neumann examples on a scalene triangle and on a planar slit domain, and reinterpret a known Dirichlet example of Dixon, Miah, Safronov, Snyder, Vakaryuk, and Wyman through the same framework.

title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
abstract: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;Λ^k\right)$, where $Λ^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this article, with one global higher integrability assumption on $du$, we study the global higher integrability of $dv$ where $v$ is the unique minimizer of the following functional: \begin{align*} \overline{w}\mapsto \int_{B} \left \lvert d\overline{w} \right \rvert^p \text{ where } \overline{w} \in u+W^{1,p}_{d^*,T}\left(B;Λ^{k}\right). \end{align*} As a machinery, with a similar higher integrability assumption on the $k+1$-differential form $\widetilde{F}$, we prove one local higher integrability of $d\widetilde{W}$ where $\widetilde{W}\in W^{1,p}\left(B_r\left(0\right);Λ^{k}\right)$ weakly solves: \begin{align*} d^*\left(\left \langle G \left(d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right), d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right \rangle^{\frac{p-2}{2}}G \left(d \widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right)\right)=0 \text{ in } B_r\left(0\right), \end{align*} for $G:B_r\left(0\right)\rightarrow GL\left({n\choose k+1};\mathbb{R}\right)$ symmetric, bounded, and uniformly elliptic measurable map, which is sufficiently close to the identity map $I:Λ^{k+1}\rightarrow Λ^{k+1}$. For each of the above mentioned cases, we prove one strong $\left(q,q\right)$ type estimate. As the primary tools, we use the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality, Fefferman-Stein inequality, and one classical regularity result of K. Ulhenbeck.

title: Testing Cross-Sectional Dependence in Clustered Data
abstract: In clustered data, cross-sectional dependence within clusters can be characterized as weak, semi-strong, or strong. This paper proposes a simple test to identify the specific nature of this dependence in linear regression models. By exploiting the variation in cluster sizes, our approach detects the underlying dependence structure in a computationally simple and robust manner. We develop a test statistic that is shown to be asymptotically chi-square distributed under the null hypothesis of weak dependence. Simulation studies and an empirical illustration using India's Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) data for 2022-23 demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed test.

title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.

title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain. Code and data will be made publicly available.

title: Offline-First Quantized AI: Design and Evaluation of an On-Device Maternal-Health Assistant for Low-Connectivity Environments
abstract: Offline language models could extend access to maternal-health information where internet connectivity is unreliable, but deployment requires both clinically appropriate responses and feasible local execution. This study presents an offline Android assistant integrating ready-made quantized language models, a clinically validated local knowledge package, conversational context, and model-initiated local retrieval. Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.5 0.8B were compared across 45 conversations and 312 turns per configuration, including a dedicated offline agentic benchmark. Gemma achieved higher response-quality, context-retention, and safety scores; Qwen offered faster generation and lower memory use. Clinician assessment of 150 Gemma responses across nine clinical domains yielded a mean quality score of 3.80/4, with 147 responses meeting the acceptance criterion. A paired RAG-on/off experiment evaluated 74 questions: retrieval improved 11 responses, left 56 neutral, produced four adverse response changes, and left three pairs unassessable. RAG-on had descriptively higher mean usefulness, safety, correctness, and actionability in the conditional 70-pair subset excluding the four flagged pairs from both conditions. Physical-device testing demonstrated offline responses on a 6 GB Android handset, with a 14.3 s median latency, alongside successful reconnection synchronization in the integrated application. Together, the findings document clinical response quality and practical performance of the integrated offline maternal-health assistant.

title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

title: Dirichlet problems and Green functions for the octonionic Monge--Ampère equation
abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the octonionic Monge-Ampere equation on smooth bounded domains in the octonionic plane $\mathbb{O}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^{16}$. For a smooth positive density that is nondecreasing in the unknown function, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution whenever there is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic subsolution with the prescribed boundary values. The result also holds on relatively compact domains with smooth boundary in flat translation quotients. On smooth bounded strictly octonionic pseudoconvex domains, we construct the unique Green function with zero boundary values and singularity $-|q-a|^{-6}+O(1)$ at an interior pole $a$. We prove $C^{1,1}$ regularity locally up to the boundary away from the pole, together with sharp bounds for the gradient and the full real Hessian. The proof combines boundary estimates based on translations and spin rotations with weighted estimates obtained by differentiating along rotations and dilations.

title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
abstract: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should be chosen as $H_{\min\{m,n\},\max\{m,n\}}(r)$ for $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$, and as the preimage of $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ under the Glaisher correspondence for $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$.

title: GEM-MM: Reducing VLM Hallucination with Entropy-Guided Preference Alignment
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are routinely aligned with offline pairwise RLHF objectives, but multimodal preference data is scarce and treats every response token as equally informative. Under a small preference budget, pair construction becomes nearly irrelevant: standard DPO-style, image-conditional, and self-improvement objectives all perform within 1.1 points on MM-RLHF metrics and 0.5 points on hallucination rates, matching the SFT baseline. We call this entropy-blind preference optimization: the learning signal ignores policy uncertainty, which in chain-of-thought VLMs concentrates on specific fork tokens where visual claims are made. We introduce GEM-MM, extending entropy-guided preference modeling to VLMs. It samples on-policy candidates, rewards high-entropy reasoning forks, penalizes uncertain final answers, and updates the model via group-normalized policy gradients. On a 3000-prompt MM-RLHF budget with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, GEM-MM achieves the best entropy-depth preference score (61.7% vs. 57.3-58.4% baselines) and implicit-reward accuracy (41.4%). Crucially, it reduces AMBER hallucination from 23.4-24.0 to 20.6 and CHAIR from 5.0-5.1 to 4.6 at matched caption coverage. It also ranks best on all three HallusionBench granularities, with a conservative operating point raising the near-chosen rate to 62.4%. An off-the-shelf multimodal reward model ranks GEM-MM first, and two such models independently confirm our main ablations (p < 0.001). We report confidence intervals, paired significance tests, metric-reward functional overlaps, and document a collapse mode when exceeding the fair budget. Code and evaluation harness: https://github.com/SNOWTEAM2023/GEM-MM

title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.

title: Projective Models of Genus 21 K3 Surfaces
abstract: We construct projective models for general primitively polarized K3 surfaces $(S,h)$ of genus $21$ (degree $h^2=40$) inside the 12-dimensional fine quiver moduli space $X = N(3;3,4)$ parameterizing stable representations of the $3$-Kronecker quiver with dimension vector $(3,4)$. As a corollary, we show that the corresponding moduli space $\mathscr{M}_{21}$ is unirational and prove O'Grady's generalized Franchetta conjecture for genus $21$. Then we investigate the geometry of $(S,h)$ through its Fourier--Mukai partner $S' = M_{S}(4,h,5)$ and construct an explicit isomorphism $f : S^{[2]} \xrightarrow{\sim} S'^{[2]}$ together with a common closed embedding into the projectivization $\mathbb{P}^{17}$ of the space of global sections of the normalized universal bundle, using the polarization $H_2 - 4δ_2$. Finally, we identify the Brill--Noether locus $\mathfrak{B} = \{Z \in S^{[3]} : h^0(F \otimes I_Z) \ge 2\}$ scheme-theoretically with the $\mathbb{P}^2$-bundle $Y' = \mathbb{P}_{S'}((F')^*)$ and exhibit an isomorphism $S^{[3]} \xrightarrow{\sim} M_{S'}(3,h',6)$.

title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, indicating that the bad experiences carry decision-relevant information. At the local level, for 47 decisions shortly before a failure of SKIP or NEUTRALIZE, removing or neutralizing a small group of bad experiences, with a median size of one, caused the trained agent to select the failing policy's action in 46 cases. For this agent, the results indicate that its decisions can be explained by its bad experiences.

title: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
abstract: This thesis investigates the expressive power of neural networks for structured data, focusing on graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures. We present four main contributions. First, we characterize the generic expressive power of geometric message-passing neural networks on sparse graphs and introduce EGenNet, an architecture achieving the corresponding guarantees. Second, we use representation theory to characterize linear layers equivariant to multiple permutations, including wreath-product symmetries. Third, we study permutation-invariant set representations that preserve containment, establish dimensional bounds and impossibility results, and introduce MASNet. Finally, we propose FSW-GNN, a message-passing architecture combining strong expressivity and bi-Lipschitz stability guarantees with strong empirical performance on long-range graph-learning tasks. Together, these results provide a broader understanding of how neural architectures can preserve the geometric, algebraic, order-theoretic, and metric structure of their inputs.

title: FastGRN: Few-Step Generative Refinement Networks
abstract: Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) generate an image by repeatedly re-predicting and refining every token of a discrete latent. They reach high fidelity, but need dozens of Markov steps. We therefore train few-step GRNs on the distribution of their own samples. We use its own uniform-state corruption to perform distribution matching on discrete tokens, which lets a discrete generator learn by backpropagation, and we pair noise with samples in the manner of rectified flow. We find that the steps of a few-step GRN do not carry the same amount of information or the same repair load. We therefore exploit its discrete refinement during training and build few-step GRNs in three parts. Oversampling samples the student with more steps than it was trained for and refines its judge on these samples. Non-uniform sampling trains only the last step and hands it most of the information at sampling time. Refinement confidence keeping holds on to the tokens the student is already sure of. We train a fast class-conditional generator on ImageNet 256 and, with the same method, a 2B text-to-image model. On ImageNet 256, the 3-step FastGRN beats the FID of GRN. On a 2B binary-token text-to-image GRN, a 4-step student also nearly matches the GenEval of GRN-T2I 2B.

title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
abstract: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

title: Two approaches of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift
abstract: We investigate the problem of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift of the form: $X_t=μt + σB_{H,λ}(t)$, for all $t\geq 0$. Based on discrete observations of $X$ and by using the method of moments with the ergodic theorem, we construct estimators of the drift parameter $μ\in\R$ and noise parameters $ σ^2,H,λ\in(0,\infty)$. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators, including convergence in probability, almost sure convergence, and asymptotic normality. Finally, by using Gladyshev's results \cite{gladyshev1961new} we provide some consistent alternative estimators of $σ^2$, $H$ and $λ$, when $μ=0$ and $H\in (0,1)$.

title: Weighted unit equations in cyclic cubic orders
abstract: We study nonrational integral units $u,v$ satisfying $au+sv=1$, with integers $1<a<s$, in varying cyclic cubic fields. The ratio $u/v$ generates the joint order $R=\mathbb{Z}[u,v]$ and gives effective finiteness for each fixed first weight and each fixed gap. Consecutive weights yield exactly seven simultaneous-isomorphism classes, at $a=2,4,13$; in every proper order among them, $\{-1,u,v\}$ generates $R^\times$.

title: acuSimNet: Multi-View Self-Occlusion-Awared Visibility Learning for Cranio-Cervical Acupuncture Points
abstract: The localization of acupuncture points (acupoints) in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) presents unique challenges since they are defined by abstract principles rather than distinct anatomical landmarks. Existing approaches are typically constrained to single view or rely on indirect calculations of relative positions with respect to other landmarks, thereby overlooking human anatomical variations. Furthermore, acupoint visibility assessment, which determins whether points are occluded by human itself, hair, clothing, or other objects, has received limited attention in practical applications. Acupoint localization itself does not require 3D reconstruction, but inferring their occlusion relationships with anatomical surfaces does, which adds computational cost and limits real-time inference. In this work, we introduce acuSimNet, an efficient hierarchical multi-task learning architecture for multi-view, self-occlusion-aware visibility prediction of acupoints, achieving 99.97% accuracy on the validation set. Our approach also addresses the challenges of high-dimensional classification (174 acupoints in cervicocranial region), negative convergence issues for visible acupoints, and inter-task scheduling optimization, resulting in substantially accelerated convergence. We improved the training efficiency from the exisiting methods of 3000 epochs to achieve 99% validation accuracy, to our optimized framework achieving 90% accuracy in 39 epochs and 99% accuracy in 86 epochs. This architecture overcomes the limitations of existing methods, could enable practical applications in acupoints detection and visualization, advancing the automation of TCM.

title: The Grid's Own Language: A Common Information Model Layer for LLM Grid Assistants
abstract: Assistants built on large language models (LLMs) are entering power system operation. Current designs delegate computations to validated solvers, but the agent still infers the type, role and state of each element from its name and tool-specific formats, and errors propagate to every study. The Common Information Model (CIM), the IEC standard in which operators already exchange network models, defines unambiguously what each element is and how it connects. We propose a CIM layer for LLM grid assistants and implement it in CONDUCTOR, an open-source assistant. Both the agent and its power-system studies read the layer. It labels the provenance of each fact (stated in the data, suggested only by a name, or inferred from topology), loads operators' CGMES models directly, and builds in $\leq$1\,s on the 9,241-bus PEGASE network. Deterministic checks compare every answer with solver results and the layer. On 37 tasks about the CIGRE medium-voltage and IEEE 30-bus networks, the agent gets right 97\,\% of the graded facts with the layer, such as a unit's energy source or a switch's normal state, against 55\,\% without it. We argue that a CIM layer should be a default component of grid assistants.

title: Stochastic Multivariate Taylor Measure Functions
abstract: We introduce stochastic multivariate Taylor measure functions (SMTMFs), which extend the multivariate Taylor measure function framework through random Taylor coefficients and a possibly random Taylor parameter. We establish their measurability properties and derive sufficient conditions for the associated processes to be martingales, including criteria based on conditional covariance and continuous semimartingale decompositions. We construct standard Brownian motion as an almost surely uniformly convergent limit of finite SMTMFs using the Levy-Ciesielski representation. We also show that the completion of the finite stochastic MTMF space under the expected uniform norm contains Brownian motion, Brownian bridges, fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with integrable initial conditions. Our main result characterizes this completion as the Bochner space, under an admissibility condition on jointly measurable stochastic Taylor coefficients. The proof uses dyadic piecewise linear interpolation to approximate integrable continuous stochastic processes in the expected uniform norm. Thus, the completed SMTMF space encompasses the full class of integrable continuous random functions on a compact time interval.

title: Dependence measures as spectral risk measures
abstract: For a bivariate copula $C$ with $(U,V)\sim C$, the conditional distribution functions $L_t=\partial_1C(U,t)$ are random variables with means $t$, so that measures of directed dependence become risk functionals. The absolute Lorenz curves of the variables $L_t$ form the rearranged copula $C^\uparrow$. In this picture Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ is a squared Sobolev seminorm and the rearranged Spearman correlation an $L^1$ norm of $C^\uparrow-Π$, and both arise from one spectral risk measure, applied either to the conditional laws of $V$ or to the laws of $L_t$. The resulting classes $ω_ϕ$ and $κ_ϕ$ of spectral dependence measures have mirror-image axiomatic properties. For every spectrum we determine the exact upper bound of $κ_ϕ$ in terms of $ξ$, and we prove sharp inequalities between $ξ$, $κ_ϕ$ and the values of $C^\uparrow$, which show how little global measures say about the tails. For plug-in estimators based on the empirical checkerboard copula we obtain consistency, rates and a resolution limit, and a simulation study shows that tail-localised measures separate copulas with identical $ξ$. An application to large credit portfolios illustrates the results.

title: Dynamical frames through Sz.$-$Nagy$-$Foias dilations
abstract: We present a unified operator-theoretic treatment of dynamical frames based on defect operators, Stein equations, and the Sz.-Nagy-Foiaş dilation theory of contractions. An explicit realization of the minimal isometric dilation relates generating vectors to the wandering subspace and provides a geometric interpretation of standard frame constructions. For Parseval dynamical frames, polar decomposition yields a complete factorization of the generating families through the adjoint defect operator. General dynamical frames are described in terms of positive solutions of a Stein equation, leading to an equivalent formulation of the frame index. We also collect characteristic-function criteria for strong stability and joint strong stability. In the diagonal case, the characteristic function expresses the classical separation and Carleson conditions in operator-theoretic terms. The emphasis is on explicit constructions, direct proofs, and a common framework for known results.

title: High-Dimensional Approximate Factor Models with Score-Driven Dynamics: Estimation and Inference
abstract: We propose a factor model for high-dimensional time series where the dynamics of the latent factors is generated by a multivariate score-driven model, thus allowing to model nonlinearities and heavy tails in both the conditional mean and the conditional variance. Estimation is in two steps: first the factors are extracted via Principal Components and then the parameters of the score-driven model are estimated via Quasi Maximum Likelihood based on the estimated factors. Since factors are not identified, we first establish set-consistency and asymptotic normality for the estimated parameters governing their dynamics, as both the number of time series and the sample size diverge to infinity. Then, we construct valid asymptotic prediction intervals, which do not depend on the chosen identifying constraints for the factors. Numerical results confirm the goodness of our estimator.

title: Towards Agentic Scientific Discovery in Distributed Systems
abstract: We investigate when adaptive tool selection helps identify a shared equation across clients with different input coverage. Query-ATLAS (query-conditioned Agentic Tool-based Learning for Aggregating Symbolic Equations) uses an LLM to guide symbolic search from client errors and previous proposals in a simulated distributed system. A four-architecture comparison reveals task-dependent opportunities: relative to fixed PySR-LLM, validation acceptances rise from 3/12 to 7/12 on CRK3 and from 11/12 to 12/12 on oscillator2, while MatSci3 favors the fixed workflow. Across 72 settings in a post-hoc six-task subset of eight development tasks, Query-ATLAS achieves 64 validation and 64 in-distribution passes, versus 62 and 59 for the fixed workflow; both pass 47/60 eligible out-of-distribution tests. The fixed workflow retains lower median errors and cost. Broader query coverage emerges as a promising benefit, motivating task-aware tool selection and client-aware fitting for scientific agents.

title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
abstract: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.

title: The Hidden Methodological Layer: Uncovering Threats to Validity in LLM-Assisted Empirical Software Engineering
abstract: Context: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in empirical software engineering (ESE) workflows, supporting tasks such as classification, coding, extraction, synthesis, and evaluation. Their probabilistic and opaque behavior, however, introduces methodological concerns that may affect empirical rigor. Aims: This paper investigates threats to validity introduced by LLM-assisted empirical workflows and examines how LLM interactions influence empirical studies. Method: We conducted a secondary analysis of 50 primary studies comprising 69 LLM-assisted research tasks identified through a systematic literature review. We examined the extent to which LLM-related threats were reported, how these threats were characterized, and how they related to established validity dimensions. Results: LLM-related threats remain substantially underreported. We identified recurring threats including classification errors, prompt-dependent interpretation, workflow instability, evaluator bias, downstream propagation of outputs, and model dependence. These threats can affect multiple validity dimensions depending on where and how LLM outputs enter the workflow. Conclusion: We introduce the concept of hidden methodological layer as a conceptual lens for understanding how LLMs influence empirical software engineering workflows. We argue that rigorous LLM-assisted ESE requires making prompts, model configurations, interaction protocols, validation procedures, and downstream reuse of LLM-generated outputs visible as part of the research method.

title: EchoSpec: Training Search Agents to Weigh Evidence Above Echoes
abstract: Search agents trained with reinforcement learning decide what to retrieve, when to search again, and when to answer. In real corpora, one claim is copied and paraphrased across many pages while the primary source settling a question appears once. We show that reinforcement-learned search agents grant echoes the credence of independent sources and lose their ability to abstain. Across five base models from 3B to 32B and seven released RL agents on multi-hop Wikipedia questions with primary evidence intact, eight paraphrased false-claim echoes overturn 58-73% of previously correct answers, while exact-match RL drives deleted-evidence abstention below 15%. Conditioning on retrieval localizes the failure to evidence acquisition: once primary evidence enters context, agents overrule eight echoes as reliably as one, whereas echoes fill top ranks and halt search early, so larger budgets, forced search turns, or passive passage filtering alone fail to recover displaced evidence. We introduce EchoSpec, specifying reliability across five corpus transformations with known target answers and training in two stages. Verification warm-start teaches multi-hop bridge-entity recovery past echoes, after which group RL optimizes an evidence-gated $λ$-reward with an outcome-independent acquisition bonus and scale-preserving advantages retaining the optimal rule $λ/(1+λ)$. Across Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Llama-3.1-8B backbones on nine evaluation suites, EchoSpec cuts eight-echo deference by 30-44 points on Qwen2.5-7B down to 29-31%, nearly quadruples eight-echo reach to 26-27% with zero-shot transfer to unseen BGE and BM25 retrievers, and raises standalone QA precision to 47-55%. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/unihsy/EchoSpec.

title: U-HamGNN: a universal model for magnetic Hamiltonians conditioned on spin and Hubbard U
abstract: The electronic structure of a magnetic crystal depends jointly on its spin configuration and the on-site Hubbard correction U, requiring a separate DFT+U calculation for each combination. We introduce U-HamGNN, an equivariant network that takes these two inputs directly and predicts spin-resolved Hamiltonians across diverse crystal chemistries. A spectral-hybrid optimizer that weights each update direction by how consistently the gradient points along it reaches 8% lower Hamiltonian error than Muon and 26% lower than AdamW in a ten-epoch benchmark. The predicted bands reproduce U-dependent gap opening and altermagnetic spin splitting within the trained window and beyond it; exchange couplings and magnetic-order calls derived from the Hamiltonian agree with DFT+U on a calibration set. This universal model provides a new tool for magnetic research.

title: Machine Learning for Near Real-Time Identification of Wildfire Burned Areas
abstract: In this article, we present a near real-time method that estimates burned probability anywhere in the world using satellite images. Our approach takes advantage of the state-of-the-art pix2pix model to translate a preprocessed index calculated from Landsat 8/9 images into an approximate of USGS Burn Probability indicating per pixel burn probability. Since this is a machine learning-based approach, it can be automated with a minimum amount of human intervention with significantly less time delays and geographic restrictions compared to other contemporary methods. We include results from our experiments and compare our approximation with the USGS Burn Probability using RMSE score.

title: Fundamental groups of closed four-manifolds with positive biorthogonal curvature
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a group is the fundamental group of a closed, connected, oriented smooth four-manifold admitting a metric of positive biorthogonal curvature if and only if it is finitely presented. This answers a question of Bettiol. The manifold can be chosen to be stably parallelizable, hence spin with vanishing signature, and with Euler characteristic $2(1-p+q)$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of generators and of nontrivial relators in a given finite presentation. Moreover, we show that the class of closed oriented four-manifolds admitting positive biorthogonal curvature is closed under surgery along embedded circles. As applications, we obtain metrics of positive biorthogonal curvature on the boundary of every compact oriented five-manifold that has a handle decomposition with handles of index at most two, which includes every oriented $S^2$-bundle over a closed oriented surface. We also obtain such metrics on $Y\times S^1$ for every closed orientable three-manifold $Y$ of positive scalar curvature and, after connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$, on a large class of four-manifolds with arbitrary fundamental group. Finally, we show that for the fundamental group of a finite aspherical two-dimensional complex $X$ the minimal Euler characteristic of such manifolds equals $2χ(X)$.

title: Reduced-Order Quadratic Representation of Higher-Order Nonlinear Dynamical Systems for Phononic Frequency Comb Generation
abstract: Phononic frequency combs arise from nonlinear interactions between vibrational modes, and their formation can be affected by nonlinearities beyond quadratic coupling. We consider a driven two-mode system near a $2{:}1$ internal resonance and examine polynomial interactions through sixth order. Through analytical derivation, we found that any higher-order nonlinear dynamical system can be expressed as a reduced quadratic framework. In the near-resonant reduced model, it has been shown that the odd-order nonlinear terms modify the effective modal frequencies, while the even-order terms modify the quadratic coupling coefficients. We assessed the accuracy of the reduced-order quadratic representation through numerical simulations using an illustrative set of parameters representative of a MoS$_2$ resonator. Numerical onset boundaries identify force--frequency regions supporting frequency combs, while Fourier spectra reveal phononic comb sidebands around the driven and subharmonic frequencies. The Long and Short equations reproduce several common trends, although differences remain in the spectral distribution and in some numerically sensitive onset estimates. These results show how higher-order nonlinearities affect comb formation and help define the useful range of the reduced description.

title: IsaGraphLib: Formally Verified Efficient Graph Algorithms in Isabelle/HOL
abstract: We present a library of formally verified graph algorithms in Isabelle/HOL. The library covers the main problems of combinatorial optimisation on graphs: reachability, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, matching, maximum flow, and minimum-cost flow. The algorithms in the library use most of the standard algorithm design techniques: graph search, greedy algorithms on matroids, dynamic programming, augmenting paths, blossom contraction, blocking flows, push-relabel, scaling, the primal-dual method, randomisation, and certificate checking. The library has adaptors between different types of graphs (directed, undirected, multigraphs), which allow results to be reused. Each algorithm is verified independently of its data structures, and the main algorithms are refined to efficient imperative implementations, from which we generate code in Standard ML, Scala, and Go. We developed parts of the library with large language models (LLMs), improved the quality of their proofs with a method based on statistics of our own proofs, and labelled which parts were developed by humans, by LLMs, or collaboratively. We perform a detailed experimental analysis of representative algorithms in our library, comparing it with state-of-the-art mainstream libraries, showing that our implementations are practical.

title: Simple abelian varieties with prescribed endomorphism ratio
abstract: Let $A$ be a simple abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, and set $m(A)=2\dim A/[\operatorname{End}^0(A):\mathbb Q]$. We prove that, for every prime $p$ and every positive rational number $μ$, there exist simple abelian varieties of characteristic $p$ with endomorphism ratio $μ$, both of $p$-rank zero and of positive $p$-rank. In particular, we answer a question of Oort in a stronger form. Our construction combines Honda-Tate theory with explicit deformations of $p$-divisible groups using Breuil windows. An explicit Frobenius matrix, realized in a window with quaternionic multiplication, gives two reduced generic slopes with coprime denominators. Their coprimality, together with specialization and constancy of dimension, determines the full geometric endomorphism algebra. Polarized Serre-Tate theory and Grothendieck algebraization lift these deformations to abelian schemes. A related construction with an additional etale factor yields the positive-$p$-rank result.

title: Dynamics and stability of volatile thin liquid films on a heated vertical cylinder
abstract: Volatile thin liquid films flowing down heated vertical cylinders are central to many heat transfer applications, including evaporative condensers, cooling of electronics, and solar thermal systems. Despite their importance, the coupled dynamics of evaporation, thermocapillarity, and interfacial instabilities on cylindrical geometries remain poorly understood. In this work, a lubrication-based model is developed to capture the nonlinear evolution of a volatile thin film under gravity, surface tension, van der Waals forces, and non-conservative evaporative flux. The model incorporates hydrodynamic pressure contributions to evaporation, enabling a unified description of phase-change effects on curved substrates. A linear stability analysis of the model equation is performed with a non-constant base film thickness. The linear growth rate is first obtained for a spatially uniform film. Then, for a spatially nonuniform film, a coupled system of linearized equations is solved using the finite element method. Further, the full liquid-vapor interface is numerically simulated to demonstrate liquid evaporation. Results reveal that evaporation accelerates film thinning, condensation promotes thickening, and van der Waals forces stabilize ultra-thin films by preventing rupture. The influence of Bond number, wavenumber, and pressure-dependent flux laws on droplet formation and collision dynamics is quantified. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into phase-change driven instabilities in cylindrical thin films and have direct implications for the design of efficient thermal management systems, evaporative cooling devices, and surface-engineered heat exchangers.

title: On the planar four-junction solution to a vector-valued Allen-Cahn system
abstract: This paper concerns entire minimizing four-junction solutions to a two-dimensional Allen-Cahn system with a four-well potential. In a suitable regime of unequal surface tensions, the construction yields a family of solutions with varying opening angles of phase sectors. The proof employs two-direction slicing arguments for tight energy bounds and localization of the diffuse interface, together with a new iteration scheme that controls change of approximating sharp interfaces at successively smaller scales.

title: A Graph Theory Assisted Method for Determining Limiting Probability Distributions of Higher Order Markov Chains
abstract: This paper presents a graph theory assisted method that checks a sufficient condition for the existence of the limiting probability distribution of a higher order Markov chain and identifies this distribution when the condition is satisfied. This method is more effective as compared to the direct verification of the condition since the latter hinges wholly on computations of the full spectrum on a large-size transition matrix. Even though the graph theoretic tools employed here are well known, their utilization in the context of a higher order Markov chain is new. This method is also implemented as an easy-to-use MATLAB function {\tt gtam}. Several illustrative examples are provided too.

title: A Dataset for Misogyny Detection in Polish Social Media: Transferability of Hateful Speech Detection from General to Specific Types of Hate
abstract: Harmful language detection is commonly evaluated on broadly defined hate speech and toxicity benchmarks, yet it remains unclear whether models that successfully detect harmful language in general can transfer this capability to more specific forms of hate. We investigate this problem for misogyny detection in Polish, an area for which dedicated resources remain scarce. We introduce a new dataset of Polish social media comments annotated for misogyny, gender-directed hateful speech. Using this resource, we first assess the reliability of LLM-assisted annotation and then evaluate general-to-specific transfer by comparing models trained on general harmful language data, safety-specialized models, and models fine-tuned directly for misogyny detection. Our results show that strong performance on general harmful language detection does not transfer uniformly to misogyny; safety-specialized models demonstrate substantially stronger generalization ability. The study contributes a new Polish resource for gender-directed harmful language and demonstrates that the scope and granularity of prior safety training are important factors in transferring harmful language detection from general to specific forms of hate.

title: Security of Deep Research Agents: Attack Surface, Defenses, Benchmarks, and Agenda Seeding against Research Planning
abstract: Deep research and agentic search agents autonomously retrieve content from the open web and generate reports with citations, and their outputs are often taken directly as research conclusions. This paper systematizes security research in this area along four stages, namely retrieval, planning, evidence integration, and report generation. We present a unified threat model, a taxonomy of attacks and defenses, and a review of evaluation benchmarks, and we align the area dimension by dimension with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) poisoning, prompt injection, and generative engine optimization (GEO). Coding 34 primary studies shows that only 26.5% of them involve the planning stage, and none performs an end-to-end poisoning evaluation on commercial products. To address this gap, we propose the agenda seeding attack, in which the attacker writes no instructions and only introduces a fictitious evaluation metric. Across 3,520 sandboxed research runs under the same budget, GEO and prompt injection are nearly ineffective, whereas agenda seeding makes the attacker's target the top pick in 16% to 28% of reports. Injection detection and query anchoring fail against it, verification prompting hurts utility, and our proposed provenance tagging preserves utility but can be bypassed by multi-site bait. Finally, we propose eight research directions.

title: Isometries for Hilbert's metric on vector lattices of continuous functions
abstract: In this paper Hilbert's projective metric on the interior of the positive cone of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong order unit is studied. We show that every surjective isometry between two such projective cones is induced by a lattice isomorphism, possibly composed with the inversion map, and that the inversion occurs precisely when the vector lattice is a bounded inverse closed $f$-algebra. In particular, two such projective cones are isometric if and only if the underlying vector lattices are lattice isomorphic, and we determine the corresponding isometry groups. We apply these results to spaces of Hölder continuous functions, absolutely continuous functions, and continuous functions of bounded variation, for which we describe the surjective isometries explicitly. Finally, we show that the projective cones of these spaces of functions on an interval all have the same metric completion, but that no two of them are isometric.

title: CleanRoute: Reconciling DRC Compliance, Post-Layout Performance, and Runtime in Analog Routing
abstract: Automated analog routing remains a long-standing challenge because design-rule checking (DRC) compliance, post-layout performance preservation, and runtime reduction are difficult to achieve together. Existing analog routers have limited coverage of joined-metal design rules, lack control over topology-induced mismatch, and face a trade-off between DRC violations and runtime on uniform routing grids. In this paper, we introduce CleanRoute, an analog router that reconciles these three targets. Hierarchical rule enforcement assigns DRC checks and repairs to stages where the required geometry is complete, covering rules both between separate metal and where metal joins. IR-drop isolation constructs supply trees from current-mirror relationships and device currents to reduce topology-induced mismatch that geometric matching cannot eliminate and voltage drops along high-current paths. A flush-line grid adds net-specific lines aligned with device-metal edges to a coarse routing grid, providing DRC-compliant connections without uniform refinement. Experiments on ten operational transconductance amplifiers (OTAs) in a commercial 40nm process show that CleanRoute produces DRC-clean and functional layouts that pass layout versus schematic (LVS) checking on all benchmarks, with the strongest overall performance preservation and a median routing runtime of 8.82s, whereas the baselines produce no DRC-clean layouts.

title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_ξ(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $ξ\in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_ξ(W)$.

title: The Frontier Must Grow - Self-proposed, interpreter-labelled training roughly doubles a 4B model's accuracy on a fresh exam as its verified frontier grows
abstract: A model can learn from problems it poses itself when an executable oracle supplies the answers. Qwen3-4B proposed Lua 5.1 programs; those it predicted wrong at least once in four samples joined a pool labelled by the interpreter, each round adding twice as many programs as the last (300, 900, 2100 in total), and each round trained a fresh adapter from the base on the pool. On the original exam the procedure met its registered criterion, an item-level test of each adapter against its predecessor. On a 2340-item exam drawn afterwards, accuracy rose from 8.3% to 16.7%; that follow-up's registered criteria were not met because round 1 gained nothing, while rounds 2 and 3 added 5.0 and 2.9 points on average, both intervals above zero. One fit on the same amount of base-proposed frontier data reached 14.6%, so the rounds' 2.1-point advantage is inconclusive. Three earlier registered series met no per-lineage criterion, and the same loop showed no gain on repository tasks or for a 27B agent in those configurations.

title: Clinician Assessment of Laryngeal Disease with Auditory AI before Laryngoscopy: A Paired Reader Study
abstract: Background: Before laryngoscopy, clinicians assess the likely cause of hoarseness and whether to suspect a precancerous or malignant lesion. Whether voice-based artificial intelligence (AI) supports pre-laryngoscopic categorization is unknown. Methods: We developed an auditory large language model that generates a patient-level assessment card (provisional category, voice-quality ratings, and rationale) and a prespecified malignancy alert from voice recordings, patient information, and acoustic measures obtained before laryngoscopy at one center. We evaluated both in a held-out test set and a later cohort. In a sequential reader study, 32 otolaryngology clinicians categorized held-out cases without AI and, 1 to 2 weeks later, reviewed their initial categories with the card (without the alert). Results: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31). Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect. Provisional-category accuracy was 72% in held-out testing and 67% in temporal validation. The malignancy alert flagged 85.7% and 86.8% of precancerous or malignant lesions. Sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions increased from 53.9% to 75.0% after AI-assisted review (difference, 21.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.3 to 42.0). Conclusions: In this single-center study, clinicians' pre-laryngoscopic categorization accuracy was higher after reviewing the AI assessment card, although the sequential design cannot fully separate AI assistance from reassessment; gains depended on model correctness without clearly selective adoption. Randomized and external evaluations, including of the malignancy alert, are needed.

title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
abstract: Let $ϕ_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|ϕ_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. We prove that $(H_N)_{N\geq1}$ is tight, uniformly over all box sizes. More precisely, for every $a\geq0$ and $N\geq1$, \[ Φ\!\left(-a\sqrt{\frac{2}{\log2}}\right) \leq\mathbb{P}(H_N>a) \leq4\exp\!\left\{-2^{-29}\frac{a^2}{\log(2+a)}\right\}, \] where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The upper bound yields uniform polynomial moments and a uniform exponential moment of $H_N^2/\log(2+H_N)$. For the upper bound, we compare a marked loop-soup exploration with a graph in which independent site variables open incoming edges. We then estimate connections in a massive field using two auxiliary vertices and bound the Gaussian remainder when the mass is removed. The lower bound uses a Gaussian translation inequality and a square-shell estimate for the Dirichlet energy, without using the massive-field argument. In particular, a height independent of $N$ gives any prescribed crossing probability below one, whereas every fixed finite height has a uniformly positive failure probability.

title: Weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift: process limits, estimated weights and efficiency
abstract: Weighted split conformal prediction handles covariate shift by reweighting calibration scores with the likelihood ratio $v=dQ_X/dP_X$; its training-conditional coverage is a functional of the self-normalized weighted empirical distribution function $\hat F_m$, and we study the process $\sqrt m(\hat F_m-F_Q)$. It converges in $\ell^\infty$ to the Gaussian process $W(G(t))-F_Q(t)W(K^2)$, with $G(t)=\mathbb{E}_Q[v\mathbf{1}\{S\le t\}]$ and $K^2=1+χ^2(Q\|P)$, if and only if $χ^2(Q\|P)<\infty$ (for non-degenerate scores); $\sup v$ plays no role. The limit gives the joint law of the coverage across levels, consistent bootstraps, inflations asymptotically exact uniformly in the level, and Berry-Esseen-type rates. With estimated ratios, a uniform expansion remains valid when the estimate uses the calibration covariates; the estimation error enters through a covariance term that can reduce the variance below the oracle's, and a pairs bootstrap reproduces it. When the ratio is known, the weighted conformal threshold is semiparametrically efficient if and only if the ratio and the coverage indicator are uncorrelated under the test distribution, with an explicit efficient correction otherwise. When $χ^2(Q\|P)=\infty$, the ratio has a regularly varying tail of index $p\in(1,2)$ and the score decouples from it in the far tail, the finite-dimensional limits are $p$-stable at the rate $m^{1-1/p}$ up to a slowly varying factor.

title: Hardware-Aware Realization of Deterministic Quantum-Walk Search on Complete Bipartite Graphs
abstract: Complete bipartite graphs offer a canonical platform for deterministic quantum search with quadratic speedup. We report the first experimental realization of deterministic discrete-time quantum-walk search over complete bipartite graphs, enabled by high-fidelity operations and a dynamical-phase compensation scheme, using a digital gate-based processor rather than an evolution-based platform. By compiling the search circuits to the native gate set and square-lattice topology, we implement full-space encoding to realize instances of graph sizes $N = 4$ and $8$, with success probabilities of 97.6% and 70.8% for finding the marked vertex, respectively. We also realize resource-efficient exact instances up to size $N = 16$, the largest achieving 66% success probability. Separately, a reduced invariant-subspace encoding preserves the dynamics of the deterministic search algorithm on two qubits for nominal problem sizes up to $N = 256$, with the success probability approaching 50%. Resource analyses of logical, hardware-compiled, and fault-tolerant-gate-set-synthesized circuits show that circuit depth and size scale as $\sqrt{N}$, with hardware overheads entering only as constant prefactors. For application-scale graphs ($N \sim 10^5$), an effective gate-fidelity model requires per-gate infidelity near $10^{-7}$. These results establish a concrete algorithm-to-hardware pathway for deterministic structured quantum search on gate-based quantum processors.

title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
abstract: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks ($Φ$SpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present $Φ$SpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. Compatible C-grid operators on spherical Voronoi meshes define a computational graph that retains non-polynomial operations and advances the state through recurrent neural integration compiled with JAX. Analytical benchmarks characterize numerical errors, and global and coastal experiments closely reproduce reference solutions generated using the Model Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) model. At approximately 14~km global resolution, A100, H200 and B200 GPUs attain 9-, 19- and 34-fold higher timestep throughput than a 96-core MPAS-SW CPU reference under matched workloads. These results extend training-free neural integration beyond polynomial dynamics to complex geophysical simulation, establishing a computational foundation for subsequent adjoint-free ensemble estimation of physical and neural parameters and informative adaptation of operator structure.

title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
abstract: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $μ$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $μ$) admit a common minimal model.

title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
abstract: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

title: The role of turbulent jet dynamics on contrail formation from conventional and sustainable aviation fuels
abstract: Large-eddy simulations (LES) coupled with a discretised population balance equation (PBE) are used to quantify the effect of turbulence on the early stages of contrail formation (jet regime) for both conventional (soot-rich) and sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs). SAFs typically have low aromatic content which causes a shift in the dominant nucleation pathway. The contribution from soot (non-volatile particulate matter, nvPM) is reduced, while the contribution from volatile particulate matter (vPM) is increased. The computational domain reproduces an experimental jet configuration that replicates the thermodynamic conditions encountered in the upper troposphere. The LES-PBE simulations capture well the jet-core cooling and bracket the experimental values of ice-crystal characteristics (number concentration, mean diameter and mass density) if a range of judicious values for parameters not specified in the experiments are employed. With the aid of one-dimensional, one-way coupled PBE approach, it is shown that soot particle activation can be reliably captured using steady aerosol-jet models. On the other hand, volatile particle activation is significantly affected by large fluctuations in temperature and humidity (and thereby supersaturation). Further downstream, non-linear dynamic coupling between the gas and aerosol phases becomes increasingly important for ice-crystal growth as well. Overall, the results demonstrate that for SAFs, turbulence is an important driver of particle activation and subsequent ice crystal growth and cannot be neglected. This finding motivates more fundamental studies to assess how turbulent jet dynamics modulates contrail formation in realistic engine configurations.

title: SWAN-Rx: Efficient and Bandwidth-Scalable Neural Reception for MIMO-OFDM
abstract: We present a Scalable Windowed Axial-attention Neural Receiver (SWAN-Rx) for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. The receiver improves reception accuracy and reduces forward-pass computation while supporting frozen-weight reuse across bandwidth allocations and channel conditions. It combines a common resource-element representation of received observations and pilot context with alternating time-axis and local frequency-axis attention. Shared parameters and relative positional information permit soft detection across allocation lengths without inference-time parameter updates. At fixed subcarrier spacing, model configuration, and symbol count, bounded frequency neighborhoods give linear growth of forward-pass computation with bandwidth. Evaluations compatible with the 5G New Radio physical layer reuse weights trained on four physical resource blocks (PRBs) at up to 273 PRBs and on unseen channels. At the training bandwidth, SWAN-Rx achieves lower pre- and post-decoding bit error rates than the implemented three-step neural receiver (NRX) and DeepRx-MIMO baselines, with 16.9% and 39.7% fewer parameters and 56.3% and 35.7% fewer forward-pass operations, respectively. The same weights achieve lower pre-decoding error rates than these baselines throughout the evaluated bandwidth-extrapolation and 16-PRB channel-transfer tests, with an estimated 0.4-0.9 dB signal-to-noise ratio reduction relative to NRX at a pre-decoding error rate of $10^{-2}$ in the 16-PRB tests.

title: Controllability of Acoustic Waves by Point Sources: Reachable States and Stable Reconstruction
abstract: We study the terminal controllability of the three-dimensional acoustic wave equation driven by finitely many fixed point sources, with zero initial data and time-dependent amplitudes supported in a finite interval. Although finitely many fixed sources cannot control the whole energy space, we establish the following results: (i) For source amplitudes in the first-order Sobolev space in time, the terminal state has finite energy if and only if all amplitudes vanish at both endpoints of the control interval. (ii) We derive an exact frequency-domain identity for the terminal energy involving a Gram matrix whose diagonal entries are one and whose off-diagonal entries are given by the sinc function, depending on frequency and source separation. (iii) For every positive control time, the terminal control operator is bounded below and is an isomorphism onto its closed reachable range, which has infinite codimension even among states satisfying the finite-propagation support condition. (iv) We establish a necessary and sufficient radiation-field criterion for reachability, provide stable reconstruction of the unique controls, and characterize the best approximation of non-reachable targets. The optimal coercivity constant equals one before the shortest source travel time. At long times, it decays as the inverse square of the control time for two sources and as the inverse fourth power for three equally spaced collinear sources. We also obtain upper bounds for general configurations and illustrate the theoretical results through reproducible Galerkin computations.

title: Communication-Efficient Distributionally Robust Federated Averaging with Multi-Source Data
abstract: Federated learning trains a shared model from distributed client data. The deployment risk is typically specified through two approximations: each unknown local distribution is replaced by its empirical distribution, and the unknown deployment mixture across clients is replaced by empirical or prescribed training weights. Existing robust methods usually address one approximation at a time through local distributional ambiguity sets or worst-case client mixtures. However, joint treatment of both approximations remains underexplored. To address this gap, we construct a global ambiguity set formed by admissible mixtures of client-wise Wasserstein ambiguity sets, yielding a distributionally robust optimization formulation. The construction allows client-dependent ambiguity radii, preserves client-wise separability of the objective function, and yields a high-probability out-of-sample guarantee for the resulting robust problem. We then introduce a penalty-based approximation of this formulation and develop a communication-efficient algorithm called BiDRO-FedAvg, for which we establish a convergence guarantee. We validate the proposed framework through a market-demand prediction simulation.

title: Turning Errors into Successes: Designing LLM Tutoring Around Scaffolded Error Correction
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) could make personalized tutoring available at scale, but it remains unclear how they can best support the instructional processes that make one-on-one instruction effective. We compared two ways of using LLMs after students make errors: providing personalized explanations of those errors, or engaging students in additional cycles of scaffolded practice and feedback, with a Socratic tutor guiding students toward the correct answer.
